..
(Today through next Saturday)

WEATHER PATTERN OVERVIEW: Main concern in the near term will be
continued gusty west-northwesterly winds across Elko County thru 
this morning as an upper shortwave continues to pass thru the 
intermountain west from the northwest, clipping northeast Nevada.
The strongest winds will be situated across the northeast quadrant
of Elko County and wind gusts in excess of 45 mph will be present
across the high terrain. Gusts will be more modest across the
valleys, peaking around 35 mph. Weather will otherwise be fair 
today with winds easing this afternoon as a transient upper level
ridge progresses through the region from the west behind the 
shortwave. Fair weather continues thru most of Sunday under the
influence of the ridge. Temperatures remain warm today and
tomorrow with daytime highs residing in the upper 40s to upper 
50s, which is around ten degrees warmer than normal for this time 
of year. 

The next Pacific storm system will begin to move into the PacNW
from the southwest on Sunday with the trailing frontal boundary
moving into Nevada late Sunday afternoon and evening. This kicks 
off a period of active weather for next week as a more progressive 
pattern sets up across the western U.S. The front moving into
Nevada Sunday will be relatively modest and warm, bringing light 
valley rain and mountain snow to northern Nevada while central 
Nevada remains mostly dry. Snow levels will be around 7000 feet 
Sunday night. Significant accumulation is not anticipated and 
valleys look to observe around 0.10 inches of rain or less. 
Southwesterly winds will also be elevated throughout the region 
with gusts 20 to 25 mph. 

There will be a brief lull in activity Monday before the next
round of precipitation begins to move in Monday night and early Tuesday.
This is indicated to be a stronger event than Sunday though the
trajectory of the system itself is indicated to be from the 
northwest, and remaining offshore before shifting east into 
SoCal. This will spread valley rain and mountain snow in the 
forecast area from the west-southwest. Given the west-
southwesterly trajectory of the precipitation, the greatest 
accumulation will be observed across central Nevada. A colder air 
mass concurrently moving in from the northwest as the parent upper
level trof moves inland will gradually lower snow levels thru 
Tuesday night and Wednesday. Snow levels are currently indicated 
to reside between 4,500 and 6,000 feet by sunrise Wednesday with 
the lower end of the range situated over Humboldt County and the 
higher end of the range over White Pine County. This will produce 
light snowfall accumulation, typically around one inch or less 
across the valleys. Otherwise rainfall and liquid equivalent 
snowfall accumulations will again be around 0.10 inches across 
northern Nevada with between 0.10 and 0.25 inches forecast across
central Nevada. Breezes will also be present. Activity clears 
from northwest to southeast Wednesday. 

There is still low confidence the latter half of the week though global
models are coming into better agreement. Another transient ridge
looks to pass thru the western U.S. Thursday and Friday bringing
fair weather before the next round of unsettled weather arrives
this weekend, potentially as early as Friday night. Though given
the low confidence, will maintain at least a low probability of 
precipitaton in the forecast for the latter half of the week at 
this time. However, dry conditions and fair weather are currently 
favored as noted. 

FORECAST CONFIDENCE & DEVIATIONS: Confidence is high with regard
to gusty winds within Elko County this morning and fair weather 
thru most of Sunday. Confidence is also high pertaining to light 
showers within northern Nevada early next week, beginning Sunday 
evening. Low confidence in the forecast outlook for the latter 
half of the week. Minimal deviation from NBM/WPC forecast but did 
increase lee side winds across Elko County thru this morning to 
better align with current observations and the short term 
forecast.
